items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: there was a trombone player named Chuck Maxon with Chico Marx’s band... So we kind of hung out because his wife and my wife became very good friends.

ctx.x: He gets married, he goes back to the hotel and all the guys show up at this thing and they go down and they hear Louis Armstrong.

I’ve got a picture here of that, when we did that scene. I’ve got a picture in the book. It was strange, I’ll tell you. But it was great, and funny, when I did get married, and I told my father we got married and he gave me a can opener. He said, “here, you’re going to need this?” I said, “what are you kidding? My wife’s going to be a great cook.” Because she had never cooked before. She was a dressmaker and she used to go to work every day, and she used to come home and her mother had dinner for her see? He says…

wife were married ten years, and he was old hand at being on the road. So we kind of hung out because his wife and my wife became very good friends. And she’d say, “don’t stay in the hotel,” the whole band would go in the hotel — he’d say we won’t stay in the hotel, we’ll stay in hotels with — what do they call them, kitchenettes. You know because we’re going to be in each town for a week. So rather than just spend rent money, we could cook and you’d save some money. And my wife learned how to cook that way. It…
